Daeun did not thank him. “That number belongs to you now, {name}.” The empty guarantee field received a NOT USED mark. The lower limit, his name, and Daeun's refusal remained on separate lines of one page.

choices.text: Remove the clauses Sangchul could not verify independently and make a new self-name copy.
choices.result_text:
{name} separated the gray-marked clauses from the contract. Sangchul said the recalculation might cross tonight's lock.

The day's chance weakened, but proposal and review did not merge into one claim. Daeun's name appeared nowhere on the new copy, and the empty guarantee field closed. The fresh paper from the printer was thinner and carried none of the unverified lines.

choices.text: Close the guarantee appendix and request a new estimate using no name but his own.
choices.result_text:
{name} removed the empty guarantee appendix and asked Sangchul to rewrite what his name alone could support. Sangchul entered a lower amount and a later deadline.

No one replaced Jaehyuk's absence. Daeun took back her refusal original. {name} lost the backup document and the day's speed. NOT APPLICABLE remained in the consenting-party field of the new estimate.

title: A Refusal Kept in Three Copies
description:
After the meeting, three separate pages lay on the copier. Daeun's original held her explicit refusal and date. The self-name reduction showed the place her name had left and NOT USED in the empty guarantee field. Sangchul's review sheet kept the clauses he had not verified in gray.

The blocked chat had stopped at its last bubble, and the guarantee attachment field remained blank. {name} kept Daeun's refusal, removal of her name, and Sangchul's unknowns on separate pages. Only the unsigned corners of the three sheets overlapped in the copier glass. As it cooled, the mouths of three clear envelopes faced different directions.

choices.text: Preserve the refusal original, self-name reduction, and unverified-clause sheet in separate envelopes.
choices.result_text:
{name} placed Daeun's refusal before her, the self-name reduction before himself, and Sangchul's unverified-clause sheet at the center. He wrote only the document title and preservation time on each envelope.

None of the three envelopes bore a new signature or guarantee number. Daeun took her envelope. Sangchul did not sign the center one. Only the copy marked NOT USED in the guarantee field remained in {name}'s hands, reflecting the copier light.

title: Only Two People at the Filing Counter
description:
Only {name} and the clerk stood at the filing counter. The blue pen was tethered by a short chain. Of the three clear envelopes, only a copy of Daeun's refusal original lay on the comparison surface. The smaller self-name filing said NOT APPLICABLE in the consenting-party field and NOT USED in the guarantee field.

The clerk moved between the refusal date and the erased name field. The screen showed both a field where Daeun's erased name could be reentered and a HOLD WITHOUT FILING button.

Neither Daeun nor Sangchul was present. What could remain now was one of four physical states: withdrawal, self-name filing, reentry of the name from the refusal copy, or an unfiled hold.

choices.text: After checking Daeun's refusal, withdraw today's filing.
choices.result_text:
{name} lowered the blue pen. The clerk stamped WITHDRAWN and read the nonrefundable fee and the counter's closing time.

Daeun's name was never entered, and the smaller self-name form was not filed. While the red stamp dried, {name} kept the refusal copy and empty consenting-party field in separate envelopes. The counter number sounded once more.

choices.text: Remove every Daeun document and file only the smaller form in his own name.
choices.result_text:
The clerk retained Daeun's refusal only as a comparison record and removed it from the filing stack. {name} reread NOT APPLICABLE and NOT USED in the guarantee field, then signed in his own name.

Filing number 227 and the date stamp landed on the smaller form. The limit was lower; no other signature appeared. The clerk offered two copies. {name} put one in his own envelope and the second in a clear envelope with no address.

choices.text: Copy the name from the refusal sheet into the erased name field again.
choices.result_text:
{name} copied the name from the refusal sheet into the erased name field again. “Do you have a current consent original?” the clerk asked. Only the refusal copy lay on the comparison surface.

Instead of a final stamp, the clerk marked CURRENT CONSENT CHECK PENDING. A temporary number appeared, but the completion time stayed blank. The clerk preserved the refusal copy and entry screen together in the hold record. The question remained aimed at an empty chair.

choices.text: Sign nothing and take the smaller form away in an unfiled state.
choices.result_text:
{name} closed the screen without pressing submit. The clerk wrote only the deadline on the unstamped form and returned it.

It was neither withdrawal nor filing. Daeun's name had not been used, but {name}'s had not entered the signature field either. He placed both copies in an envelope and stepped away. The blue pen's chain swayed over the empty counter.

title: The Second Envelope Without an Address
description:
Two copies of the smaller self-name filing carried the same number 227 and date stamp. The consenting-party field said NOT APPLICABLE, the guarantee field said NOT USED, and {name}'s name appeared once in the signature line.

One entered his own clear envelope. He placed the second in a separate envelope that could have gone to Daeun, but left the recipient line blank. His last chat with Daeun remained open on the phone, its input field empty.

Only the filing time remained between the addressless envelope and the empty input field. The choice in his hands was to preserve the unsent copy and its time as they were.

choices.text: Do not send the second envelope. Mark only UNDELIVERED, the time, and filing number.
choices.result_text:
{name} wrote UNDELIVERED and the current time at the upper right instead of filling the recipient line. He left the phone's input empty and turned the screen face down.

The face-down screen faintly reflected the ceiling. One copy stayed in his envelope; its twin remained in a desk drawer. When the drawer closed, a corner of the clear plastic caught briefly, then folded inside.

title: Notice of Money That Did Not Move
description:
After the execution deadline, Sangchul's seven-page original remained open on the desk. The balance-transfer screen showed no completion time. No cancellation stamp or assignment approval existed. Only self-name filing number 227 remained in its clear envelope.

The last call screen from Sangchul still read RESUME SIGNING AT THE ORIGINAL LIMIT. No later question or demand had arrived. {name} had to speak first.

The unsigned final page and empty transfer time remained side by side with the screen. What he could send now was that no money moved, the original remained with him, and the time of that notice.

choices.text: Tell Sangchul first that there was no transfer or execution, and preserve the open original's current time.
choices.result_text:
{name} sent: ‘I did not transfer the balance today, and the contract was not executed. I still hold the original.’ The attached photo showed only the unsigned final page and the clock.

A sent time appeared beneath the bubble, followed only by empty screen. {name} did not reopen the transfer screen. He put the original in a clear envelope, leaving the final digits of filing number 227 visible.

title: Documents to Return Instead of a Key
description:
There was no key envelope on the cafe table before Hyunsu. Instead lay self-name filing number 227, the sent record telling Sangchul there had been no transfer or execution, and the seven-page original that still had to be returned. Its final signature field and completed-transfer time were blank.

Hyunsu flattened a corner before reading the figures. “Hyung, this time you didn't hold the door with someone else's name.” He placed the filing beside the sent record. “But the time people spent reading all this didn't disappear.”

{name} opened a return-preparation envelope beside the empty place where a key might have been. As Hyunsu read the three records again as people's time, the recipient line stayed blank and the corners of all seven original pages remained outside the envelope.

choices.text: Open the filed copy, no-execution record, and original to return. Hear Hyunsu to the end.
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu read the filing number, sent time, and blank signature line. “Filing in your name and not sending the money were both things you did, Hyung. You didn't use a person as collateral, but that doesn't erase how long people waited.”

{name} offered no defense. He placed the original in a separate envelope marked RETURN PREPARED and left the recipient line blank. A cold glass of water and the unsealed envelope remained where a key might have been.

title: A Filing Stamp and an Empty Transfer Time
description:
Seven days remained until his thirty-eighth birthday. Beside the notebook where he had first written KRW 3 billion, {name} opened his self-name filing and the contract original prepared for return. The filing bore number 227, a date stamp, and his name. The execution signature and balance-transfer time were blank. There was no key.

The record of checking Daeun's refusal, Sangchul's unverified clauses, and the no-execution notice Hyunsu read remained between earlier pages. Filing had not moved the money. Not executing had not returned people's time.

Only the notebook's last line was blank. At the pen tip, the question split: under what name could he carry both the stamped choice and the contract that had not moved?

choices.text: Write that both the filing and non-execution were his choices, then sign his name.
choices.result_text:
{name} copied the filing number and sent time of the no-execution notice onto one line. Beneath them he wrote, BOTH THE FILING AND THE MONEY NOT SENT WERE CHOICES MADE BY {name}, then placed his name.

The stamp remained, but no completed-transfer mark appeared. The black name and blank execution field shared one frame. When he set down the pen, the final page of the return-prepared original lifted and settled.

choices.text: Put the filed name and missed execution time into the cost column and calculate.
choices.result_text:
{name} entered Sangchul's review time, Daeun's refusal, and the night before Hyunsu into the cost column. The filing number went under assets; the unmoved money and closed deadline went under loss.

The ledger grew more exact while people's voices shrank between figures. His name pressed long into the final line. Only the calculator's cold light remained beside the empty transfer time.

choices.text: Write first on the back of the filing the names of those who called him by name.
choices.result_text:
{name} flipped the filed copy and wrote Daeun, Hyunsu, Minseo, Sangchul, Jaehyuk, and Father in order. His own name came last.

The contract did not become executed, and the filing did not disappear. But people's time stood before the stamp and empty transfer time. {name} opened the first contact that could still answer and read one name aloud from the page.

title: The Appointment Offer Returned in Three Boxes
description:
After the closing announcement, the supervisor set a red C1 cover over C0's printed document ID and hash. Beneath the request to leave Hyunsu out of the external numerical reviewer field, the company listed three revisions: delay the appointment ten business days, lower the monthly lead-duty allowance from KRW 450,000 to KRW 300,000, or cut the task-force budget twenty percent.

“This isn't a promotion gift. It shows who carries the approval time.” He wrote the same signature deadline beside all three. C0's line saying an external name shortened approval from fifteen business days to five remained uncrossed. “Not a choice for today. Just don't pretend you missed it.”

All three losses lay open before {name}. No box held a circle or signature.

choices.text: Ask first where his title and pay remain during the ten-day appointment delay.
choices.result_text:
The supervisor drew a ruler between C1's effective-date field and current-title field. “For those ten days, your current title and current pay. You also can't sign as the person responsible before approval.”

{name} wrote the sentence in the margin. The cost of the delay was now exact in date and authority, but the lead-duty allowance and budget lines stayed open. The supervisor pushed C1 back without marking any option selected.

choices.text: Confirm what the difference between KRW 450,000 and KRW 300,000 becomes over twelve months.
choices.result_text:
The supervisor turned the calculator around: KRW 150,000 a month, KRW 1.8 million over twelve months. “The KRW 6 million training-cost clawback is separate. Lowering the lead-duty allowance doesn't erase that liability.”

{name} marked the two amounts on different lines of C1 instead of merging them into one cost. The effective date and budget did not change. Only the lead-duty allowance difference became a clear figure he might lose now.

choices.text: Have the supervisor read which work disappears if the budget is cut by twenty percent.
choices.result_text:
The supervisor pointed in turn to the external-verification fee and temporary staffing hours in the spending table. “It isn't only money. You'll reconcile the figures yourself, and the team will split the work.”

{name} wrote people's time beside both lines. It was an option that increased time inside the company instead of borrowing Hyunsu's name. The lead-duty allowance and effective date remained unselected beneath C1.

title: The Corner Folded at the End Date
description:
Minseo reread C1 from the beginning. The first page stayed white. Her blue pen stopped at the final page's KRW 6 million training-cost clawback. She underlined BEFORE TWELVE MONTHS and folded the corner at the sentence defining its end: midnight on the day twelve months after the actual effective date. A delay to the appointment would move that end with it.

The external numerical reviewer field held no person's name. Minseo wrote CONFIRM NOT USED beside it and put different question marks on the KRW 300,000 lead-duty allowance option and the twenty-percent budget cut.

“I can't stamp this safe. I can separate the day it ends from the lines no one has answered.” She wrote the review's start and end times on the cover and turned the full C1 back toward {name}.

choices.text: Take back the full C1 with Minseo's blue marks and review times intact.
choices.result_text:
{name} did not flatten the folded corner at the end date. The external numerical reviewer field with no person's name, CONFIRM NOT USED, and the question marks beside the lead-duty allowance and budget amendments went into one file unchanged.

Minseo wrote only the return time, not her name, in the receipt field. “In the next room, don't merge the line I found with the supervisor's answer.” When the clear file closed, one blue mark remained visible beyond the cover.

title: Four People Reading the Same C1
description:
Three copies bearing the same hash as the C1 original lay open. The supervisor held the approval schedule, Minseo the blue-marked copy, and Hyunsu the external numerical reviewer page. {name} had no paper; disclosure meant watching all three turn pages from the same distance.

The supervisor set his watch beside the deadline. “Without an external name, the company spends ten more days. In return, one of these three costs stays on your side.”

Minseo pressed the repayment end date. “If the effective date moves, does this move?” Hyunsu looked at the field that had nearly held his name. “Hyung, if you meant to use my firm's name, first tell me what I would remain on record as reviewing.”

Three questions were open. The review could begin on only one line.

choices.text: Let Minseo question the supervisor directly about the repayment end date first.
choices.result_text:
Minseo read C1's effective date beside the repayment end date. The supervisor answered that both moved only under the appointment-delay option; the original effective date held under the lead-duty allowance and budget options.

Minseo put a blue check only beside the answered sentence. Hyunsu's name field remained blank. {name} had not selected a loss. Only the supervisor's watch hand moved across an empty box in the approval schedule.

choices.text: Have all four read the external numerical reviewer field on Hyunsu's copy first.
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu read the fine print beneath the field aloud. An external name would be recorded as the person who had verified the figures and their basis. “That isn't glancing at one table. If it's wrong, that name follows me back to my job.”

Minseo boxed the verification-scope sentence in blue and asked whether internal review could replace it. The supervisor said yes, at the cost of ten more approval days. The field remained unfilled.

choices.text: Put the three amendments on one line and ask who carries each loss.
choices.result_text:
Minseo wrote THE TITLE HELD BY {name} beside the delay, THE MONTHLY PAY OF {name} beside the lead-duty allowance cut, and THE TEAM'S TIME beside the budget cut. The supervisor did not erase any of them.

Hyunsu placed a finger beneath the external-name field. “Using my name reduces these, but gives me the verification liability. Correct?” The question moved from numbers to people. Every selection box on C1 remained empty.

title: C2 Before the Filing Stamp
description:
At 9:42 p.m., C1 held Minseo's blue marks, the field Hyunsu had indicated, and the meeting time. The external numerical reviewer field held no person's name. The supervisor opened a new file titled C2 REVISION INSTRUCTION.

“External name: NOT USED. Responsible party: SELF ONLY.” He pointed to three empty boxes: delay the appointment ten business days, lower the monthly lead-duty allowance from KRW 450,000 to KRW 300,000, or cut the task-force budget twenty percent. “One box must show which cost stays on your side.”

Hyunsu said, “Hyung, not using my name is the starting point. You choose who loses what instead.” Minseo checked that the repayment end date had carried over. Tonight produced only a public revision instruction; every filing-number and company-stamp field stayed blank.

choices.text: Leave a C2 revision instruction lowering the monthly lead-duty allowance from KRW 450,000 to KRW 300,000.
choices.result_text:
{name} wrote KRW 300,000 in the lead-duty allowance field and ruled once through KRW 450,000. The external numerical reviewer became NOT USED, the responsible party SELF ONLY, and the repayment end date stayed in the same place as on C1.

The supervisor read the monthly KRW 150,000 difference. Minseo checked only that figure. Hyunsu folded the empty name field on his copy once, then flattened it. The C2 cover received UNSIGNED / UNFILED. There was still no filed company record.

choices.text: Leave a C2 revision instruction delaying the appointment by ten business days.
choices.result_text:
{name} moved the effective date ten business days forward. Minseo moved the repayment end with it and wrote the new date formula. The external numerical reviewer closed as NOT USED and the responsible party as SELF ONLY.

The supervisor confirmed that his current title and approval authority would remain for those ten days. Hyunsu's name remained outside the document, but the waiting time moved to {name}. Only the revision-instruction time, not a stamp, remained on C2.

choices.text: Leave a C2 revision instruction cutting the task-force budget by twenty percent.
choices.result_text:
{name} removed twenty percent from the spending-table total. The supervisor said the choice between external-verification fees and temporary staffing hours would still have to be made after launch. Minseo left question marks on both unresolved lines.

The external numerical reviewer became NOT USED and the responsible party SELF ONLY. Hyunsu's professional name remained outside the document, but the team still faced a loss of time. A copy of the unsigned C2 went to each of the four people.

title: Four States at the Company Counter
description:
The counter's blue pen hung from a short chain. The clerk read the unsigned C2's KRW 300,000 monthly lead-duty allowance, repayment end date, and SELF ONLY. The external numerical reviewer field said NOT USED; a small edit control remained beside it.

The C2 revision-instruction time left by the four people was present, but no filing number. Withdrawal would end C2. Filing it would leave his name alone. Copying Hyunsu's name and firm from the saved contact would place it in intake without external verification. A hold would leave every stamp blank.

The supervisor, Minseo, and Hyunsu were absent. Whether the public promise became a company record split again where no one could decide for him.

choices.text: Withdraw C2 and close today's filing window.
choices.result_text:
{name} closed the submission screen and chose withdrawal. The clerk stamped the unsigned C2 cover WITHDRAWN with the time. The external numerical reviewer field still said NOT USED, but the self-name appointment packet was not filed either.

The KRW 300,000 lead-duty allowance and repayment end date did not become executed terms. {name} left with one withdrawal copy. When the next number sounded, only the blue pen moved above the empty signature surface.

choices.text: Remove every Hyunsu record and file only the self-name C2.
choices.result_text:
{name} reread NOT USED in the external numerical reviewer field and SELF ONLY as responsible party, then signed his own name. The clerk placed document ID TF-C2-SELF, a filing stamp, and the time on the same first page.

The monthly lead-duty allowance remained KRW 300,000 and the repayment end date stayed exactly as written on C2. The clerk returned two copies bearing the same ID. One went into {name}'s clear file; the other into a separate envelope to hand directly to Hyunsu. The external numerical reviewer field held NOT USED; the verification-signature line stayed blank.

choices.text: Secretly restore Hyunsu's name from his saved contact in the external numerical reviewer field and submit it.
choices.result_text:
{name} opened the edit control and entered Hyunsu's name and accounting-firm line. The clerk read the warning that no external verification statement was attached and accepted it as PENDING REVIEWER VERIFICATION. A provisional ID and input time appeared, but no final stamp came down.

NOT USED had disappeared, and there was no consent document from Hyunsu. The approval period had not shortened to five business days. Only the lettering copied from the contact remained on the pending screen.

choices.text: Leave C2 unsigned and take it away unfiled.
choices.result_text:
{name} chose not to submit. The clerk wrote only today's filing-window close on C2 and returned it. NOT USED and SELF ONLY remained on paper, but there was no filing number or effect.

The withdrawal-stamp box and reviewer edit-input field were both empty. {name} placed the unsigned C2 in its envelope. The blue pen's chain brushed his hand, and only his turn vanished from the number display.

title: The Second Copy by the Revolving Door
description:
The accounting firm's revolving door moved departing workers one shoulder at a time. Hyunsu came down wearing his badge. {name} handed him the clear envelope holding the second TF-C2-SELF copy. One page showed the KRW 300,000 lead-duty allowance, repayment end date, external numerical reviewer NOT USED, and responsible party SELF ONLY.

Hyunsu checked the name field first and pressed his lips together. Between lobby announcements came only the sound of a paper corner flattening. The copy slid between notebooks in his bag.

{name} entered the document ID and handover time. The record ended at that time; the next line stayed white. When the door revolved again, only the empty envelope remained between them.

choices.text: Place the filed copy directly in Hyunsu's hands and record only its ID and handover time.
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu matched TF-C2-SELF to the filing stamp, then put the copy inside his bag. {name} saved the time on a delivery screen with no confirmation-signature field and turned the phone face down.

Their employee badges briefly overlapped in the revolving-door glass, then separated. Hyunsu's bag zipper closed. {name} retained only his own filed copy and the handover time.

title: The Name Left Behind the Blank Field
description:
At the late cafe, Hyunsu left his TF-C2-SELF copy closed and placed his firm badge face down. “Hyung, I saw that my name was left off the paper.”

{name} set out his filed copy and Minseo's blue-marked review sheet. Hyunsu drew the blue-marked end date closer. “While you calculated that my name made it five days, I didn't know what I would be recorded as reviewing. A firm name isn't lettering you erase. One wrong table could follow me into my next job.”

The ice before {name} had nearly melted. The clean NOT USED field proved the filing state. It did not erase Hyunsu's time and professional boundary before the field was closed as NOT USED.

choices.text: Close the filed copy and hear Hyunsu to the end.
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu described where his time had gone, from the day his name was first raised to the lobby where he received the copy. “Not using it in the end was your choice, Hyung. The time I spent waiting for that choice was mine. Write down both.”

{name} kept his hand still on the filed copy. He waited for Hyunsu's sentence to end as the last ice melted. Hyunsu put the copy in his bag and set his cold glass on the return counter. One sheet for a next date stayed blank on the table.

choices.text: Explain first that the final filing did not use Hyunsu's name.
choices.result_text:
{name} pointed from NOT USED to his own signature. Hyunsu looked at the sheet, then put his badge back around his neck. “I know the result. I'm asking why my name was a shortcut to you in the first place.”

The clean field became evidence in a rebuttal, and the conversation shortened. Hyunsu put the filed copy in his bag and stood. The note field for the date his name was first raised stayed blank before {name}.

choices.text: Ask Hyunsu to define the boundary sentence they should use from now on.
choices.result_text:
When {name} offered a blank notepad, Hyunsu did not take the pen. “If I write your company's rule too, you're putting my time in the review field again.”

He pressed only NOT USED on his copy. “You write the next sentence. Ask me then if you need to—don't put my name up first.” The notepad returned blank to {name}. Hyunsu's boundary remained in the hand that had declined the pen.

title: Three Documents Before KRW 300,000
description:
At HR, TF-C2-SELF, an offer-decline form, and a resignation settlement lay under separate clips. “Only one thing moves today,” the supervisor said. “Execute the appointment, close the offer, or settle this job.”

Execution would create C3 with the KRW 300,000 monthly lead-duty allowance and repayment end date. A KRW 300,000 preparation payment, effective time, new badge, and old-badge return confirmation would follow. Declining left the payment and C3 blank. Resigning moved wages and unused leave as printed and ended current access.

{name}'s phone showed no deposit. Only three signature fields lay open beneath the fluorescent light.

choices.text: Sign the self-name C2 and execute the task-force lead appointment.
choices.result_text:
When {name} signed, the HR clerk stamped execution-confirmation ID TF-C3-EXEC and its effective time. A moment later his phone showed the KRW 300,000 task-force preparation deposit. The monthly lead-duty allowance of KRW 300,000, repayment end date, and external numerical reviewer NOT USED shared C3's first page.

The new access badge arrived already active in its envelope. The HR clerk dropped the old badge into the collection box and gave {name} a confirmation stamped RETURNED with its time. The supervisor said, “These figures come up under your signature now.” C3's performance-result field remained blank; only money, effect, and badge number filled today's line.

choices.text: Decline C2 and take back only the documents for his current title.
choices.result_text:
{name} signed the offer-decline form. The HR clerk stamped C2 NOT EXECUTED and canceled the task-force preparation transfer. The new-badge issue field stayed blank; the old badge remained around his neck.

The supervisor handed him one decline copy. Its next-action field ended in a blank line. The KRW 300,000 monthly lead-duty allowance and repayment end date bore NOT EXECUTED. His account screen did not move.

choices.text: Sign the resignation settlement instead of the appointment packet.
choices.result_text:
{name} verified the wages and unused-leave amounts on the resignation settlement, then signed. The HR clerk stamped the settlement-transfer time and collected his current badge. The task-force payment field and C3 ID field stayed blank.

The supervisor folded the empty badge lanyard into the return envelope. The settlement's NEXT EMPLOYER field remained blank. Only the amount printed on the settlement moved into the account. C2 was bound separately beneath a cover marked NOT EXECUTED — RESIGNATION.

title: The Time the Execution Copy Changed Hands
description:
The crosswalk between the company and the accounting firm changed twice. {name} handed Hyunsu the copy stamped with execution-confirmation ID TF-C3-EXEC. The monthly lead-duty allowance of KRW 300,000, repayment end date, NOT USED, preparation-payment time, new-badge issue, and old-badge return confirmation were bound together.

Hyunsu matched only the IDs on the first and final pages and held the copy without folding it. {name} opened the delivery record and entered the document ID and current time. Its final line ended at that time; the cursor did not move lower.

The walk signal came on again. Rather than remain in the roadway, both men crossed to the same sidewalk. The execution copy remained in Hyunsu's hands; the receipt time remained on {name}'s screen.

choices.text: Hand Hyunsu the C3 execution-confirmation copy and save only the receipt time.
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu checked TF-C3-EXEC and the preparation-payment time, then put the copy in his bag. {name} saved the receipt time and closed the screen.

“Got it.” Hyunsu pulled the bag zipper shut. When the crosswalk signal ended, both stepped away from the curb. The dark screen held the delivery time; the closed bag held the execution copy.

title: A Signature Beside the New Badge and Return Confirmation
description:
Seven days remained until his thirty-eighth birthday. Beside the notebook that first held KRW 3 billion, {name} opened TF-C3-EXEC. One page showed external numerical reviewer NOT USED, responsible party SELF ONLY, the KRW 300,000 monthly lead-duty allowance, repayment end date, and preparation-payment time.

The new badge was active. The old one sat in HR's collection box; only its RETURNED confirmation lay behind C3. Then came Minseo's blue sheet, C2's filing stamp, what Hyunsu said to the end at the cafe, and the execution-copy receipt time.

Contacts and Father's call record were closed. The badge envelope stayed sealed. Only the notebook's last line waited beneath the executed title and reduced pay.

choices.text: Copy C3's document ID and loss, then sign his own name at the end.
choices.result_text:
{name} wrote TF-C3-EXEC, the KRW 300,000 monthly lead-duty allowance, and the repayment end date on one line. Beneath them he wrote, RESPONSIBILITY EXECUTED WITHOUT AN EXTERNAL NAME BELONGS TO {name}, then signed.

The new badge stayed inside its sealed envelope, and the contacts screen was dark. The black signature, NOT USED, and preparation-payment time remained on one page. The lost KRW 150,000 a month remained in the earlier cost column.

choices.text: Separate the reduced lead-duty allowance and other people's time into cost columns, then sign.
choices.result_text:
{name} put the twelve-month lead-duty allowance difference of KRW 1.8 million under money. Minseo's review time and Hyunsu's waiting went under people. He left the total box between the columns empty.

He signed his own name on the last line. C3's effective time remained unchanged. The old-badge return confirmation held down the notebook corner and divided the columns of money and time.

choices.text: Write the names the document did not borrow, then sign his own name last.
choices.result_text:
On the notebook's final page, {name} wrote Minseo and Hyunsu as the people who had read the document and spoken a boundary. His own name and the execution time came last.

On C3 open beside it, the external numerical reviewer field still said NOT USED and the responsible-party field SELF ONLY. He left the notebook's new-badge-photo space blank. One self-signature and three different people's time remained on the final page.

title: Three Terms Beneath the Same KRW 3.2 Billion
description:
Beyond the acquirer's glass wall, office lights went dark. The acquisition lead opened SA-20, the Equity Acquisition Term Sheet. Hash 91B4 followed the non-binding letter's A6E8. The KRW 16 billion valuation, {name}'s 20%, and KRW 3.2 billion price were identical in all three packages.

The first kept {name} in transition work, the named team, and the existing service for twelve months. The second released {name} after ninety days and kept the team for twelve months, but ended the service in ninety days. The third kept {name} for ninety days and the service for twelve months, but cut the named team's continued employment to ninety days.

“The price doesn't move. Whose time gets shortened does.” No box or signature had been marked. The paper had not crossed the table.

choices.text: Open his transition-work schedule first and ask how the twelve-month and ninety-day hours and reporting lines differ.
choices.result_text:
The acquisition lead opened only {name}'s transition schedule and read the weekly hours and reporting lines. The twelve-month package kept weekly work beside a final reporting date; the ninety-day package brought the last handover date first.

The named-team and existing-service schedules stayed folded. {name} touched no selection box. Only two transition end dates and an empty signature line remained on the table.

choices.text: Open the named-team appendix first and ask what twelve months versus ninety days means.
choices.result_text:
The acquisition lead joined the two end dates with a ruler. One fell twelve months away; the other, ninety days. “Both say continued employment. After these dates, they are different promises.”

{name} wrote the number of people in a margin separate from the price. The service and transition schedules stayed folded, and no circle appeared on the team appendix.

choices.text: Open the existing-service appendix first and read what closes after ninety days.
choices.result_text:
The lead read down the service list and its end date. Under the ninety-day package came new-sales suspension, a user-migration notice, and shutdown of the operating account. Under twelve months, those three fields remained active.

{name} watched the order of the closing verbs, not the first-user count. The team list and his transition schedule stayed folded. No selection mark appeared.

choices.text: Leave without taking the review draft and end the acquisition discussion today.
choices.result_text:
{name} rose before reaching a signature line. The acquisition lead clipped the three packages into one file and wrote the meeting-end time on its cover. The KRW 3.2 billion transfer and 20% transfer fields stayed blank.

After the glass door closed, the draft remained on the acquirer's table. {name} held only a visitor-badge return slip; the acquirer's next-review field stayed empty.

title: Corners Folded at Three End Dates
description:
Minseo cut the seal on the complete SA-20 Equity Acquisition Term Sheet. The cover put previous hash A6E8 beside current hash 91B4; the body and three appendices also ended in 91B4. She recalculated 20% of the KRW 16 billion valuation, matched KRW 3.2 billion, and checked the price once.

Her blue pen stopped at three dates: {name}, twelve months or ninety days; the named team, twelve months or ninety days; the existing service, twelve months or ninety days. She boxed the line letting the acquirer determine a “substantially similar role.”

“I can't give you legal clearance. I can show whose date gets shorter under the same price.” She wrote her review start and end times, then folded each date's corner a different way.

choices.text: Take back the complete copy with Minseo's blue marks and review times intact.
choices.result_text:
{name} checked the single price mark, three end-date lines, and blue box around the role exception. No blue mark appeared in any selection box.

The full copy returned to its clear folder with the same page count. Only the three corners pointed in different directions. Hash 91B4 and the return time remained on the same screen; the signature line stayed white.

title: Four People Reading the Same Term Sheet
description:
Three copies ending in hash 91B4 lay open in the startup's small meeting room. The acquisition lead had the transition schedule, Minseo her blue-marked copy, and the cofounder the named-team and existing-service appendices. No paper lay before {name}; he had to follow the pages in three other pairs of hands and the same hash on their covers.

“The KRW 3.2 billion is identical,” the lead said. “Only where the twelve months sit remains.” Minseo pressed the boxed ACQUIRER DETERMINATION line. The cofounder pointed to the blank name field under JOINT WARRANTY. “Taking out my name and erasing what I built after three months are different things.”

Every selection box stayed empty. Only one piece of evidence could move to the table's center first.

choices.text: Put Minseo's marked role exception in the center first.
choices.result_text:
Minseo turned her copy so the blue box faced everyone. “Does this mean a role survives as long as its new title sounds similar?”

The acquisition lead said attaching the current-role list could narrow the buyer's discretion. The cofounder set a finger beside their own role. The sentence was public, but no deletion line had appeared. All three duration boxes remained empty.

choices.text: Put the cofounder's named-team list in the center first.
choices.result_text:
The cofounder read each name beside its current role and employment end date. “Don't write ‘continued employment.’ Write the Monday through which these people keep reporting to the same roles.”

The acquisition lead marked the twelve-month and ninety-day dates. Minseo boxed the undated role exception again. The joint-warranty field stayed white.

choices.text: Open the acquisition lead's transition schedule and read {name}'s time first.
choices.result_text:
The lead read the weekly hours and reporting line. Under the twelve-month package, {name}'s transition work continued every week; under ninety days, the last handover date came first.

“Read where the price of your quick exit lands on our sheet too,” the cofounder said. Minseo copied the transition end date beside the team and service dates. The three spans now stood together, but none had been selected.

title: Three End Dates Before the Stamp
description:
PUBLIC REVISION INSTRUCTION appeared above three boxes. The first kept {name}'s transition work, the named team's roles, and the existing service for twelve months. The second kept {name} for ninety days, the team for twelve months, and the service for ninety days. The third kept {name} for ninety days, the service for twelve months, and the team for ninety days. KRW 16 billion, 20%, and KRW 3.2 billion stayed fixed beside every row.

COFOUNDER JOINT WARRANTY: NOT USED and SEPARATE SELLER SIGNATURE PAGES went in first. “The starting terms for all three,” the lead said. Minseo checked the attached role dates.

{name} had to choose what shortened, not the money. Only a new-hash public revision could be created. Signature, filing, payment, and transfer fields stayed blank.

choices.text: Keep his transition work, the named team, and the existing service for twelve months.
choices.result_text:
{name} circled the first box. His transition end date, the named team's current-role end date, and the existing-service end date moved to the same date twelve months away. The cofounder warranty read NOT USED; each seller had a separate signature page.

Minseo joined the three dates with one blue line, and the cofounder checked their own role. When the lead issued revision hash D772, its cover read PUBLIC REVISION — UNSIGNED — UNFILED. The KRW 3.2 billion transfer and 20% transfer fields stayed blank.

choices.text: Keep the named team for twelve months and cut his transition work and the service to ninety days.
choices.result_text:
{name} chose the second box. The named team's current-role date remained twelve months away; his transition work and the existing service moved up to ninety days.

The cofounder folded the first line of the service list. Minseo drew a blue bracket between the two dates. The new revision held the selection time and unequal dates. Its signature line stayed white; a dash filled the filing-number field.

choices.text: Keep the existing service for twelve months and cut his transition work and the named team to ninety days.
choices.result_text:
{name} chose the third box. The service schedule continued for twelve months; his transition work and the named team's current roles ended after ninety days.

The cofounder pulled the team list closer. The acquisition lead kept the headcount out of the KRW 3.2 billion column. The shortened employment date remained on the new revision, while its execution field stayed white.

title: Four States at the Pre-Closing Desk
description:
At the acquirer's pre-closing desk, revision D772 and an onscreen comparison lay side by side. {name}'s transition work, the named team's current roles, and the existing service all ended on the same twelve-month date. COFOUNDER JOINT WARRANTY read NOT USED, and every seller had a separate signature page.

A conditional signature on his own seller page would create a pre-review filing number and two copies. The file could be returned for a date or hash mismatch. He could request forty-eight hours or withdraw. A black sign read PRE-REVIEW — NO CLOSING SERVICES.

The KRW 3.2 billion payment time, 20% transfer time, and acquirer final-confirmation field stayed blank. With neither the cofounder nor Minseo present, the public revision could become a filing under his name—or remain paper.

choices.text: Verify COFOUNDER WARRANTY: NOT USED and conditionally file only his seller page.
choices.result_text:
{name} matched revision D772 and all three dates to the comparison screen, then signed his own seller page. The clerk stamped CONDITIONAL PRE-REVIEW with its filing time and handed him two same-hash copies. One entered {name}'s folder; the other entered a separate envelope for direct delivery to the cofounder.

The cofounder's signature page remained in its own packet, and the warranty field still read NOT USED. Payment, the 20% transfer, representative-seal handover, and the acquirer's final confirmation received no stamp.

choices.text: Mark an appendix end-date mismatch and stop the filing.
choices.result_text:
When {name} opened the comparison, one digit in the uploaded service end date lit differently from the paper revision. He printed both dates and attached them to a discrepancy sheet. The clerk stamped the time under RETURN FOR CORRECTION, not the signature line.

The filing-number screen showed a dash, and the copier tray stayed empty. His seller page returned unsigned. The account screen and his 20% line in the shareholder register did not move.

choices.text: Take the revision and submit a forty-eight-hour extension request.
choices.result_text:
{name} wrote RECHECK THREE END DATES in the reason field and received a return time forty-eight hours later. The clerk slipped only the extension receipt under revision D772's cover.

{name}'s own signature page and the cofounder's separate page remained blank. No closing date or transfer reservation appeared. When the next number lit above the desk, he held only the revision and one new appointment time.

choices.text: Withdraw from the acquisition before the conditional signature.
choices.result_text:
{name} wrote the deal title and current time on the withdrawal form. The clerk punched revision D772 and bound it behind the form, then returned a shareholder-register copy that still showed his 20%.

No line appeared in the KRW 3.2 billion payment field. The cofounder warranty remained NOT USED, and the separate signature page stayed empty. When the envelope closed, the counter pen swung at the end of its short chain.

title: The Second Copy Before Closing
description:
When the startup's fire door shut, only the copier's vibration came through the wall. {name} handed the cofounder the second copy stamped with the conditional pre-review filing time. {name}'s twelve-month transition work, twelve months for the named team's current roles, twelve months for the existing service, COFOUNDER WARRANTY: NOT USED, and separate seller pages all sat under hash ending D772.

The cofounder first checked that their name appeared on a separate seller cover, not in the warranty field. They squared the paper corners once and tucked the copy under one arm. {name} entered only the document title and handoff time in the delivery screen.

Its payment and share-transfer fields were still blank. The copier stopped downstairs. One copy remained in each person's hands.

choices.text: Hand over the conditionally filed copy and record the cofounder's separate seller-page signature and return time.
choices.result_text:
The cofounder checked hash D772, NOT USED, their separate seller page, and all three twelve-month dates. They wrote their own time on the seller page, signed it, and sealed only that page in the return envelope. The remaining filed copy went into their document bag.

{name} saved the copy-receipt time and sealed return-envelope number, then closed the screen. One first copy, one second copy, and one signed page bound for the pre-review desk remained separate in the stairwell.

title: The Owner Field on the Team Briefing Sheet
description:
At the late office table, the cofounder left the conditionally filed D772 copy closed and pushed over a team briefing sheet. Beneath ACQUISITION TERMS, QUESTIONS, and ANSWER OWNER, only the last field was empty.

“I saw that you kept my name out of the warranty.” They braced the document bag against one shoe. “But while you wrote that you'd take KRW 3.2 billion and stay twelve months, these people will hear the dates on their desks from us. Don't call me protected, then make me deliver the notice.”

{name} kept the team list and briefing sheet apart. The acquisition lead meant precise contract language without a founder's face. The cofounder meant making the most affected person explain it too. His own name meant taking the next room's questions.

choices.text: Write his own name as answer owner and hear the cofounder to the end.
choices.result_text:
{name} entered his own name under ANSWER OWNER and set the first team briefing's date and start time. The cofounder began with the questions people would ask next Monday, not twelve months later.

{name} kept his hand still on the filed copy. Only after the last sentence did he pull the briefing sheet toward himself. The named-team list remained before the cofounder; the date on which he would take questions remained before {name}.

choices.text: Name the acquisition lead as answer owner and require an exact contract briefing.
choices.result_text:
{name} put the acquisition lead's title in the blank and attached all three contract end dates. The cofounder read it, then stood the document bag upright. “The contract sentences will be exact. That person still can't say why we chose to sell.”

The sheet gained an owner and date, while {name}'s name remained outside the question field. Their chairs stayed slightly apart until the light over the team list went out.

choices.text: Put the cofounder's name in the owner field and say he will stand behind them.
choices.result_text:
When {name} wrote the cofounder's name, they stopped the pen with one finger. “I can speak. I'm not also paying the price of you hiding behind me.”

They changed the field to JOINT BRIEFING and left {name}'s name on the same line. The cofounder's fingertip smudge and the pen's pressure mark remained beneath both names.

title: Three Packets Before KRW 3.2 Billion
description:
Three clipped packets lay in the closing room: 5C20 after D772, an appendix discrepancy, and a termination confirmation. The cofounder's separately signed seller page, bearing their return time, had reached the D772 packet. The acquisition lead kept the bank screen. “A match moves one transfer. A mismatch stops it. Ending leaves everything put.”

5C20 showed the KRW 16 billion valuation, {name}'s 20%, KRW 3.2 billion, three twelve-month dates, and COFOUNDER WARRANTY: NOT USED. Beside it were the 20% register line, seal tray, sealed admin token, and transition badge. The phone showed no deposit.

D772 held the conditional signature; the 5C20 line before {name} was white. He could pull only one packet closer.

choices.text: Match the conditional filing to the execution copy and sign the conforming close.
choices.result_text:
{name} and the acquisition lead matched D772 to 5C20, then checked the three end dates and NOT USED before signing the execution page. The bank screen changed once; one line for KRW 3,200,000,000 appeared on his phone. {name}'s 20% line in the shareholder register gained a transfer time.

{name} placed the representative seal in its tray and handed over the sealed top-admin token. The clerk stamped the closing time, account-closure time, and transition-badge number together. His former executive access went dark; only the transition badge lit green. No second deposit line appeared.

choices.text: Confirm an appendix-date mismatch and stop the closing.
choices.result_text:
{name} overlaid the named-team date in 5C20 with the conditionally filed copy. They differed by one day. The acquisition lead took his hand off bank approval and stamped both times on the discrepancy report.

The KRW 3.2 billion deposit line and 20% transfer time remained blank. The representative seal stayed outside its open tray, and the top-admin token remained sealed. The transition-badge field stayed white when the closing-room door opened.

choices.text: Sign the termination confirmation and retain his 20%.
choices.result_text:
{name} read the deal title and 20% holding on the termination confirmation, then signed. The acquisition lead closed the bank request and stamped NO CLOSE with its time on 5C20.

{name}'s shareholder-register line did not change. The representative seal and top-admin token returned to their original case, and no transition badge was issued. His phone showed only its pre-meeting balance. One termination copy lay under a clip separate from the execution packet.

title: The Execution Copy After the Deposit
description:
Outside the closing room, the cofounder waited with the visitor badge attached. {name} handed over execution copy 5C20 in a clear folder. Its first page showed the closing and KRW 3,200,000,000 deposit times. Behind it came {name}'s 20% transfer line, the representative-seal and top-admin-token handover, and the transition-badge number.

The cofounder checked the team's and existing service's twelve-month dates before the KRW 3.2 billion figure, then matched COFOUNDER WARRANTY: NOT USED to the separate seller page. {name} saved the title and handoff time.

The closing stamp vanished under the cofounder's arm. The deposit remained as one account line, the copy under another person's arm, and the handoff time on a closed screen.

choices.text: Hand the execution-confirmation copy directly to the cofounder and save its receipt time.
choices.result_text:
The cofounder matched hash 5C20, the 20% transfer time, and the twelve-month dates, then put the folder in their bag. {name} saved the receipt time and closed the screen.

“Got it.” The zipper closed after the short answer. The delivery record ended at the receipt time, and the phone returned to its lock screen. When the elevator opened, one person held a transition badge and the other the execution copy.

title: A First-Week Responsibility Sheet Beside the Transition Badge
description:
Seven days remained until his thirty-eighth birthday. Beside the notebook that first held KRW 3 billion, {name} opened the execution copy and a first-week responsibility sheet. Under hash 5C20 were the KRW 16 billion valuation, 20%, the KRW 3,200,000,000 deposit time, and three twelve-month dates. The seal-and-token handover confirmation, former-access closure slip, and transition badge held down the notebook.

Minseo's blue copy, the conditional filing stamp, the briefing sheet bearing the cofounder's questions, and both delivery times lay in version order. Only TEAM BRIEFING, SERVICE ON-CALL, and FOUNDER ADMIN CLOSURE CHECK had empty owner fields.

EXECUTED covered the transaction signature block. The pen before {name} pointed only to one line on the first-week sheet.

choices.text: Copy the scheduled first team briefing's owner and date onto the responsibility sheet, then sign.
choices.result_text:
{name} copied the already scheduled first team briefing's date, start time, and answer-owner name onto the first-week responsibility sheet. He attached the order for questions about the cofounder's role and the named team's end date.

He signed the responsibility sheet. The execution copy kept its deposit and 20% transfer times in their respective fields. Beside the badge, the already scheduled meeting date appeared once more on the sheet.

choices.text: Take the existing service's first on-call shift and sign beside its end date.
choices.result_text:
{name} put his name in the empty slot for the first week's night shift. He joined the existing service's twelve-month end date to the first alert-wait time on one line.

The signature appeared only on the on-call sheet. The execution stamp and bank receipt stayed unchanged; the admin token remained in the completed-handover tray. One night-call sheet entered the folder behind the transition badge.

choices.text: Sign the handover sheet that verifies closure of the founder admin account.
choices.result_text:
{name} matched the former top-admin account's last access time to the access-closure time in the execution copy. The screen split into TRANSITION ACCOUNT ACTIVE and FOUNDER ADMIN CLOSURE VERIFIED.

He signed the closure-check sheet. The screen kept the 20% transfer time, and the account kept its single KRW 3.2 billion deposit line. Beside the dark former-account screen, the transition badge lit green once.
